scenes.headline: Prompts that survive production
lines: Lesson three. Prompts that survive production.
Your instructor is Patrick Diamitani.
Clever wording isn't the trick. Structure is.

scenes.headline: Five parts that hold up.
lines: Strong prompts have five parts.
A role.
A clear goal.
Constraints, like length or tone.
Examples of what good looks like.
And the exact output format you want back.
scenes.code:
Role: Senior product marketer.
Goal: Launch copy for the pricing page.
Constraints: Under 120 words. No hype.
Example: see docs/voice.md
Output: 3 headlines + 1 paragraph.

scenes.headline: Write it like a brief for a smart colleague.
scenes.sub: Point to files instead of pasting them in.
lines: Put together, it reads like a brief you would hand a smart colleague.
Notice the example points to a file, instead of pasting it in.

scenes.headline: Iterate. Don't restart.
lines: When the output misses, resist the urge to start over.
Say exactly what's wrong, and what to keep.
Starting fresh throws away everything the agent just learned.

scenes.headline: Plan first. Then build.
lines: For bigger jobs, use a loop.
Ask for a plan.
Correct the plan.
Execute it, one step at a time.
Then verify the result.

scenes.headline: What you just learned.
lines: Quick recap.
Fixing a plan is cheaper than fixing a product.
Your mission: rewrite one prompt you use every week, with all five parts, then run the plan-first loop on it.

takeaways.t: Iterate in the same thread — don't restart
